claims.text: Pulumi's component state migrations let component authors ship an upgrade path with the component itself; a migration translates the saved state of a component and its children before Pulumi works out which resources need to change.
Pulumi component state migrations are a new feature (recently introduced).
The Pulumi component state migrations API is experimental and may change.
A component state migrations discussion exists at github.com/pulumi/pulumi/discussions/24799.
The legacy AWSX VPC component is `awsx.classic.ec2.Vpc`; in the example's v1 it creates a VPC with one isolated subnet, a route table and association, and an internet gateway.
Replacing an AWS VPC requires replacing the security group that refers to the VPC's ID (per AWS CloudFormation EC2 SecurityGroup VpcId documentation).
The modern AWSX component is `awsx.ec2.Vpc`.
The example's third version removes AWSX and declares the resources directly with `@pulumi/aws`.
Across all three versions of the example, the AWS resource IDs stay the same and the security group continues to use the same VPC.
Pulumi state records each resource and component with a URN (Pulumi name); managed resources also have a provider ID.
Legacy AWSX wraps the subnet and internet gateway in separate components, modern AWSX removes those wrappers, and the subnet's Pulumi name changes from `vpc-isolated-0` to `vpc-isolated-1`.
Pulumi aliases handle changes to a resource's name, type, or parent when saved state remains compatible, but cannot remove component wrappers and transfer references.
Pulumi resource registration accepts a `stateMigrations` option taking a migration callback, used together with an alias for the legacy component type.

A state migration callback receives the old component's saved state followed by its children's state, and returns `newState` (complete set of replacement records) and `successors` (map from each disappearing old URN to its replacement URN).
The example's `rename` helper copies the saved record, changes its URN, type, and parent, and preserves the AWS resource ID and other saved fields.
Pulumi uses successors mappings to update dependencies and resource references elsewhere in the stack.

Pulumi runs multiple state migration callbacks in order, passing each result to the next; a legacy-AWSX stack can upgrade directly to plain AWS, and a modern-AWSX stack skips the first migration; after both have run, callbacks return no result on later updates.
After a migration, Pulumi compares the new program with migrated state and calls the provider for remaining changes; the example can still show in-place updates for provider defaults and tags.
`pulumi preview` evaluates the state migration without saving it, and the update (`pulumi up`) saves the migrated state.
When users upgrade a component that registers a migration, Pulumi runs the migration automatically as part of normal preview and update, with no user-written migration or stack state editing.
The pulumi/examples repository contains an `aws-ts-awsx-vpc-state-migration` example with v1, v2, v3 programs and migration files at v2/migration.ts and v3/migration.ts.
A docs guide exists at /docs/iac/guides/building-extending/components/state-migrations/ covering the callback contract.
Pulumi state migration callbacks (the state migrations resource option) run during previews and updates when prior state exists.
Pulumi state migration callbacks must be idempotent and must return no result when the state no longer needs migration.
Pulumi state migration callbacks rewrite state without performing provider operations.
A Pulumi component state migration callback is a pure function that transforms the saved state of a component and its children into the state expected by a new component version.

A Pulumi component state migration callback returns the updated state records and successor mappings, where each mapping connects an old URN omitted from the result to the URN of the returned resource that takes its place.
If no migration is needed, a Pulumi component state migration callback returns no result.
The Pulumi component state migration callback state entries use the checkpoint resource format, including fields such as urn, type, id, parent, provider, inputs, and outputs.
The option reference for the stateMigrations resource option at /docs/iac/concepts/resources/options/statemigrations/#callback-api explains the callback API.
A Pulumi component state migration callback that returns no result can remain attached when using update plans or targeted updates.
The restrictions on state-changing results of Pulumi component state migrations (with update plans or targeted updates) do not require removing an already-applied migration.
